name: Bikini Bottoms OffRoad Park
customer: UTV and side by side riders, mud boggers, race spectators
unique: A bottomland off road park in the Forked Deer bottoms with trails cut through mud and woods, a rock course, a bounty hill and race weekends that draw UTV classes from several states.
buzz: Riders come for the mud and stay for the camping, which is free and unpowered. The race weekends are loud, crowded and the reason the park exists.

name: Dyer County Heritage Museum
unique: A historical society museum of a county on the Mississippi bottomland, with the farm tools, photographs, uniforms and family files of the towns that grew on the river and the railroad.
buzz: Volunteers run it and the file cabinets are the real collection. People tracing a Dyer County family find more here than online.

name: Dyersburg Court Square
unique: A courthouse square in the largest town between Memphis and Jackson, with a 1900s courthouse, storefronts and a monument, in a county that still farms cotton, corn and soybeans on the old river bottom.
buzz: It is a working county seat rather than a tourist square. The stores are open, the parking is free and the lunch places fill at noon.

name: Trenton Teapot Museum
unique: A municipal teapot collection displayed in the city hall where the city conducts its business, with hundreds of pots in glass cases lining the corridors, one of the few places in the world where you pay a water bill in an art gallery.
buzz: People come expecting a joke and find a serious collection. The staff are used to visitors wandering the halls and will point out the oldest and the strangest.

name: Trenton Court Square
unique: A square with a red and blond brick courthouse in the middle, storefronts around it and a monument on the lawn, in a town that has been the Gibson County seat since the 1820s.
buzz: Well kept and easy to walk. The teapot museum is in the same block, which makes the square a twenty minute stop with a story.

name: West Tennessee Agricultural Museum
dates: Weekdays and some weekends, call ahead
customer: Farm families, equipment people, school groups
unique: A collection of the tools and machines that turned west Tennessee from forest into cotton and soybean ground, from hand tools and horse drawn plows to the first tractors, with a room of household goods from the same farms.
buzz: Farmers walk through naming the equipment and telling you what it was for. It is the kind of museum that means more to people who grew up on the land and still surprises everyone else.

name: Tennessee Safari Park
unique: A seven and a half mile drive through safari on a working farm, where zebras, giraffes, camels and ostriches come to the car window for feed, plus a twenty acre walk through with primates, reptiles and a petting area.
buzz: The animals put their heads inside the car and that is the whole review. Parents warn that the feed buckets empty fast and the ostriches are aggressive, and that children talk about it for months.

name: Davy Crockett Lake
unique: A small TWRA lake outside Alamo with a fishing pier, a boat ramp and bank access, stocked and managed for bass, bream and catfish, in the middle of the flat farmland of the Forked Deer basin.
buzz: Local families fish it on summer evenings and it is quiet on weekdays. It is not a destination lake, which is exactly why the people who use it like it.

name: Horns Bluff Wildlife Management Area
dates: Year round; hunting seasons restrict access
unique: A bluff and bottomland tract on the Forked Deer River managed for deer, turkey and waterfowl, with the kind of river swamp that covered this whole basin before the drainage ditches.
buzz: Birders work it during migration and hunters know the bottom. Wear orange in season and expect mud.

name: Carroll County 1000 Acre Recreational Lake
dates: Year round, best April to October
unique: A county built lake of a thousand acres with a swimming beach, a boat ramp, fishing piers and campgrounds, made for the people of a county that has no other big water.
buzz: Locals fish it for bass and crappie and swim all summer. It is a county park in the best sense, cheap and busy on holidays.

name: The Dixie Carter Performing Arts Center
company: The Dixie Carter Performing Arts and Enrichment Center
customer: Music and theater audiences, locals, touring acts
unique: A performing arts center named for the actress who grew up in Huntingdon and played Julia Sugarbaker on Designing Women, with a main hall that books touring country, bluegrass and theater alongside local companies.
buzz: The room is better than a town of four thousand has any right to have, and the season mixes names with local shows. People drive from Jackson for the bigger acts.

name: Huntingdon Court Square
unique: A square with a 1930s courthouse, shops and a monument, a block from the Dixie, in a town that holds a strawberry festival and a Christmas parade that people come back for.
buzz: Small, tidy and easy to walk before a show. The square is the reason to arrive early rather than at curtain.

name: Big Cypress Tree State Park
unique: The site of the largest bald cypress ever measured in the United States, a tree that stood in this low wet ground until lightning took the top in 1976, with a boardwalk and a young cypress growing beside the stump of the old one.
buzz: People come to see where a national champion stood and are surprised that the park is a quiet bottomland with a boardwalk, not a monument. Birders like the wet woods.

name: Ned R. McWherter Library and Museum
company: City of Dresden and Weakley County
unique: A small town library and museum honoring the governor who grew up picking cotton in Weakley County and later signed the legislation that created Tennessee's statewide kindergarten program, with his papers, photographs and campaign material.
buzz: It is part library and part civic memory, and the staff are proud of it. People researching Tennessee politics find more here than they expect.

name: Dresden Court Square
unique: A square with a 1900s courthouse, a ring of storefronts and the county's memorials, in the seat of a county named for a signer of the Declaration of Independence.
buzz: Quiet and well kept. The square and the museum together make an hour, which is what most visitors have.

name: Natchez Trace State Park
unique: Thirty six thousand acres of the old resettlement land between the Hatchie and the Tennessee, with two lakes for fishing and swimming, cabins, a riding stable, forty miles of trail and a shooting range.
buzz: It is the biggest park in west Tennessee and the one locals use all year. The horse trails and the lakes are the two draws, and the cabins book early.

name: Beech Lake
unique: A city lake with a sandy beach, a swimming area, picnic shelters and a campground, which makes it the summer afternoon for a county with no other public swimming water.
buzz: Parents say it is cheap, close and clean enough, and the beach is packed in July. Anglers fish the far side where the weed line is.

name: Lexington Court Square
unique: A courthouse square in a town that grew on the railroad and the timber trade, with brick storefronts, a monument and the county's war memorials on the lawn.
buzz: A working square with a diner and a hardware store. People stop on the way to the park and find the town more alive than the interstate suggests.

name: Chickasaw State Park
unique: Fourteen hundred acres of pine and hardwood ridge with Lake Placid, a swimming beach, WPA era stone and log cabins, and campgrounds that sit under some of the tallest pines in west Tennessee.
buzz: The cabins were built by the WPA and people book them for reunions. The lake is small and warm and the trails are easy, which suits families with young children.

name: Chickasaw State Forest Horse Trails
unique: Hundreds of miles of bridle trail through the state forest around the park, with a riding stable at the park that rents horses and a network of sandy ridges and creek crossings that drains well after rain.
buzz: Equestrians come from several states with their own horses and say the trail is the best in west Tennessee. Hikers share it and should expect hoof prints and the occasional loose horse.

name: Henderson Courthouse Square
unique: A square with a 1900s courthouse and a ring of shops in the county seat next to Chickasaw, in a county named for a Pennsylvania signer who never set foot in it.
buzz: It is a ten minute walk and the place to buy lunch before the park. Locals are used to campers wandering in during the summer.

name: Nathan Bedford Forrest State Park
unique: A park on Pilot Knob, the high bluff above the Tennessee River where Confederate artillery shelled a Union supply depot at Johnsonville in 1864, with a museum, a lookout tower and trails down to Kentucky Lake.
buzz: The view from Pilot Knob over the river is the best on this stretch and the museum explains the raid without glorifying it. Sunset from the tower is the local ritual.

name: Kentucky Lake at Camden
dates: Year round, best spring to fall
company: Tennessee Valley Authority and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers
unique: The southern end of a reservoir that runs a hundred and eighty four miles up the Tennessee River, with flooded timber, cypress and a spring crappie run that draws anglers from across the mid south.
buzz: Crappie anglers plan vacations around the spawn and the lake is huge enough to absorb them. Birders work the bottomland for herons and eagles in winter.

name: Camden Court Square
unique: A square with a 1900s courthouse, shops and a monument, a few minutes from the lake and the state park, in a county that trades on both.
buzz: Small and friendly, and the bait shop is the busiest place in town. People stop for lunch between the park and the water.
